name: PASADENA PERFORMANCE PRODUCTS

reports_to_state.source: TCEQ Air Emission Event Report Database (STEERS), cached detail pages

reports.cause_excerpt: Instrument Air Compressor tripped resulting in a process upset in the Dimerization and Alkylation Units with process streams being routed to the flare for control.
Emergency shutdown switch faulted resulting in valve opening to the flare to relieve pipeline pressure.
Unit lost power causing Dimer and Alky unit trips. Both Unit's process streams were routed to the flare for control.
A plugged check valve required two vessels to be cleared and subsequent check valve removal and replacement.
A process critical Compressor tripped due to faulty level indicator which resulted in upsets in the dimerization and alkylation units.
Emergency Hand switch on the dimerization ethylene feed line was inadvertently pressed causing a control valve to close. The closed control valve resulted in an increase in line pressure which (by…
Drain valve was plugged with process solids when trying to clear piping. The process solids became unplugged releasing the material to the atmosphere.
The Dimer Unit Startup did not exceed any Reportable Quantity (RQ). Pasadena Performance Products wishes to withdraw this Emission Event notification.
A third-party steam supply outage and subsequent power outage caused process unit upsets. The process unit trips resulted in the Dimerization and Alkylation Units and their process streams being…
Loss of all catalyst to the dimer unit caused a process unit upset. This upset resulted in Dimer and Alkylation units and their process streams being routed to the flare for control.

reports_to_epa.source: EPA Toxics Release Inventory via Envirofacts
reports_to_epa.note: Pounds per year, stack plus fugitive air releases; a null means the form gave no number.

caveats: Being upwind of a spike is not evidence of anything; wind at one monitor cannot tell facilities apart.
Reports listed here are what the facility reported to the state (TCEQ STEERS); amounts are the facility's own estimates.
TRI figures are what the facility reports to EPA each year for routine releases; they are estimates, not measurements, and not events.
